summary.name: Browser game (Wikipedia)
summary.one_liner: A Wikipedia article describing browser games, video games played over the internet in a web browser without installation, and their history from the 1990s through the Flash era, HTML5, and .io games.
use_cases: Learning the history of Flash games
Finding out how to play old Flash games
Researching the origins of indie browser games
Background reading on HTML5 game development
summary.what_it_does: The article defines browser games as video games played in a web browser, usually free-to-play and single or multiplayer, with no installation needed. It traces their history from early text-based games like Earth 2025 (1995), through the Flash era that Newgrounds and Kongregate shaped, to the decline of Flash after Apple's 2010 stance and Adobe's 2017 announcement. It also covers the rise of HTML5, WebGL and WebAssembly, the .io genre started by Agar.io in 2015, and Flash emulators such as Ruffle and Flashpoint preservation efforts. The page is encyclopedic and does not offer a downloadable tool.
notable: Covers the history of Flash games from 1999 onward, including Newgrounds' Pico's School
Explains the 2020 end of Flash Player support and preservation projects like Flashpoint and Ruffle
Describes the .io game genre sparked by Agar.io in 2015
Lists genres first developed or popularised by browser games, such as endless runners and social network games
caveats: Flash games now require unofficial methods such as emulators or third-party plug-ins to play outside China
Browser versions of games may have fewer features or inferior graphics than native versions
